newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends down, benchmark shift imminent.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends down, benchmark shift imminent.

text.p: The key March three-month Euroyen futures contract ended Monday's day session slightly down on position adjustment, ahead of Japan's general election.
The market is becoming cautious ahead of general elections on October 20, traders said.
"If the New Frontier Party and the Communist Party, which oppose a rise in the consumption tax, do well, that could be seen as a sell factor," a city bank trader said.
"The June was sold on position adjustment...there were no new factors today," the trader for a major brokerage house said.

The June's relatively large fall compared to the March was due purely to technical factors, and did not mean that the market's view of Japan's monetary policy had changed in any way, the trader added.
The key overnight call rate stood at 0.47 percent as of 0656 GMT, up from Friday's weighted average of 0.45 percent.
Such a rise is unusual on the day before the last day of a bank reserves reporting period, traders said.
"I think some banks probably had a large deviation from the required level of reserves," a trust bank trader said.
Strong fund demand from such banks probably led to the unusual rise in the overnight call rate, the trader said.
The BOJ injected 100 billion yen into the money market this morning, which almost offset a projected fund shortage of 110 billion yen.

About 20 billion yen worth of three-month and two-month certificates of deposit (CDs) was issued at 0.52 percent and 0.50 percent, respectively. About 80 billion yen worth of one-month CDs was issued at 0.49 percent.
